However, his family experiences a scandal: one of his grandsons, son of Joiada, marries the daughter of Sanballat, the adversary of the Jewish people, which brings disgrace upon him and provokes Nehemiah's indignation, leading to his expulsion (Nehemiah 13:28).
H0475N.origine: The name Eliashib means "God restores" or "God establishes" in Hebrew (from "El," God, and a root suggesting restoration). This name expresses the hope that God restores His people after exile and ruin. Eliashib literally embodies this restoration: he is the high priest who presides over the return of the exiles and the rebuilding of the Temple.
H0475N.emploi: Eliashib appears four times in the Book of Nehemiah, always at the heart of the events of post-exilic restoration. He is first presented in the genealogy of high priests (Nehemiah 12:10), establishing his official importance. Next, he is mentioned as a reference point for dating events: "in the time of Eliashib," indicating that he was a prominent and lasting figure in his ministry (Nehemiah 12:22). His son Johanan succeeds him (Nehemiah 12:23). Finally, the text reveals a moral failing: his family compromises itself through a mixed marriage with an enemy family, which disrupts the community restoration project that Nehemiah advocates (Nehemiah 13:28).
H0475N.portee: Eliashib reminds us that even high priests and prominent figures remain vulnerable to moral compromises and dangerous alliances. His story warns the reader that spiritual responsibilities require vigilance over not only oneself but also one's family and surroundings. It also shows that God restores His people — as promised by his name — but that this restoration depends on the faithfulness and vigilance of each individual.

sens: High priest of the temple during the time of Nehemiah
Man from the time of exile and return
H0475O.detail: Eliashib is a high-ranking priest who serves in the temple of Jerusalem during the governorship of Nehemiah. The text designates him as established in the chambers of the temple (Nehemiah 13:4). This man abuses his position by granting Tobiah, an adversary of the reconstruction of Jerusalem, a room in the temple courts (Nehemiah 13:7). His actions illustrate how even religious leaders can misuse holy places for personal and political purposes.
H0475O.origine: The name Eliashib means "God restores" (from the Hebrew "El" = God and "yashaḇ" = to restore, to establish). It carries within it the hope of divine restoration, a central theme during the time of the return from exile.
H0475O.emploi: Eliashib appears in the book of Nehemiah as a figure from the years following the return from Babylon. Although he is a priest, he does not set an example of faithfulness: Nehemiah rebukes him for allowing Tobiah, an enemy of Israel, to have a room in the temple. This episode shows the religious and political compromises that hindered the reconstruction of the Jewish community.
H0475O.portee: The case of Eliashib teaches that a religious title or position does not guarantee moral integrity. Even those called to serve God in the sanctuary can succumb to corruption and ambition. It is a call to remain vigilant and faithful to principles, regardless of one's position.

H0475L.detail:
1. Eliashib is a man mentioned during the return from exile, in the time of Nehemiah. He belongs to the lineage of Zattu and made the mistake of taking a foreign woman as his wife, which violated God's law regarding mixed marriages (Ezra 10:36).
2. The broader context shows that Eliashib represents one of the many men who, after the return from captivity in Babylon, had to repudiate their non-Israelite wives to conform to God's will and purify the people.
H0475L.origine: The Hebrew name אֶלְיָשִׁיב (Eliashib) literally means "God restores": it comes from the root שׁוּב (shûv), "to turn, return, restore," and the word אֱלֹהִים (Elohim), "God." This name evokes restoration and divine grace. Several different men bore this name in the history of Israel, including a priest under David, a descendant of David, and a high priest during the time of Nehemiah.
H0475L.emploi: Eliashib is mentioned only once in the Bible, in Ezra 10:36. He appears in the list of the sons of Israel who had taken foreign wives and who, at Ezra's command, had to repudiate them to obey the Law. This passage is part of the account of the return from Exile and the religious restoration of Israel after the Babylonian captivity.
H0475L.portee: The story of Eliashib teaches the believer that faithfulness to God involves obedience to His word, even when it requires difficult personal sacrifices. It also shows divine mercy: the people were given a chance to repent and reconcile with God after the exile, provided they accepted to return to holiness.
